finding.summary: The canonical Kata StatefulSet still uses ReadWriteOnce for both writable PVCs. Kubernetes documents ReadWriteOnce as node-scoped and explicitly notes that multiple Pods on the same node can access the volume. ClayVerse requires one canonical writable entity/state authority, so RWO alone does not close same-node concurrent-writer/split-brain risk during replacement or orchestration races.
finding.preferred_repair: Use ReadWriteOncePod for both canonical writable PVCs and make CSI/RWOP support plus negative concurrent-mount proof a final acceptance gate.
finding.authority_boundary: This changes storage attachment/fencing only. It creates no second state, identity, effect, recovery or deployment authority. UnifiedDB remains canonical.
finding.counterhypothesis: replicas=1 plus StatefulSet ordering and RWO may be sufficient in normal operation
finding.reason: RWO constrains the node rather than uniquely constraining the Pod; the desired single-writer invariant must survive abnormal replacement/race conditions, not only nominal replica count.

primary_external_evidence.fact: ReadWriteOnce can allow multiple Pods on the same node to access a volume; ReadWriteOncePod constrains access to a single Pod and is stable since Kubernetes v1.29.
Kubernetes recommends ReadWriteOncePod where strict single-writer access is required; RWOP is CSI-only and requires compatible CSI sidecars.
